cpu_microbenchmark.cpu: AMD EPYC 9V74 (container host; different from the user FPS-test PC)
cpu_microbenchmark.scope: Fabric VanillaBlockModelPartEncoder with Minecraft BakedQuad fixtures and actual Sodium meshes. Warm-cache CPU geometry conversion/replay only; excludes full extraction, tint/light calculations and GPU rendering. Not FPS.
cpu_microbenchmark.method: Four warm-up pairs, nine measured pairs, 12000 calls per mode and size; alternating order; median of measured rounds.

ci.publication_policy: A Release 0.8.0: commit on main publishes a non-prerelease after the build and actual renderer checks succeed. The publishing job verifies metadata, JAR CRC and SHA-256 before upload.

limitations: The benchmarked implementation was 0.8.0-alpha.1; all 51 production class bytes are identical in release 0.8.0, with only the version in fabric.mod.json changed.

Two 48-phase singleplayer runs on one PC used 300 item displays and 300 block displays, no custom resource pack, without shaders and with Complementary Unbound r5.9.3 High. They do not prove every pixel, custom model, shader pack, GUI interaction or reconnect scenario.
The per-frame snapshot cache was BYPASS on the tested renderer-added state; no effective snapshot cache hits are claimed.
Usable block-display local bounds were absent on the measured FRAPI/Sodium path. Item culling was observed; prepared block states did not fall. Unknown bounds remain visible conservatively.
Changing-block shader measurements showed higher average FPS but mean phase 1% low fell 64.9 to 60.0 FPS. Long frames coincide with GC pauses; more repetitions are needed.
Time and weather were not frozen, and a 75 ms first measured frame affected the first no-shader phase. Small FPS differences are indicative.
Persistent geometry caching requires optional Fabric Renderer API 17.0.16+. Mesh parity checks use actual Sodium 0.9.2; compatibility with all renderers is not established.
Geometry is replayed separately for each display; the cache does not batch draw calls or implement GPU instancing.
Generation invalidation clears retained meshes on the next cache use. Storage is bounded by entry count and 65536 quads; meshes over 4096 quads use bounded bypass markers.
The quick plan compares combined DMO options; Benchmark 1.1.0 all/geometry plans isolate this switch in their geometry groups.

limitations: The release CI runs automated checks without launching a complete graphical Minecraft client; it does not measure in-game FPS or establish compatibility with every modpack or shader pack.
Standalone Mixin application and Mod Menu API smoke checks are recorded under historical_verification for 0.7.0; they were not rerun by the 0.7.1 release workflow.
The block-model cache covers normal block_display model preparation, not all item models or GPU rendering costs.
displayRenderDistance defaults to 18 blocks. Zero preserves the original render distance, and existing explicit configuration values are retained.
Occlusion depends on the optional Entity Culling mod, including its asynchronous updates and transparency rules.
Unknown or animated item-model bounds and moving entity anchors retain visibility conservatively.
Correct visual output with the intended server resource pack and shader pack still requires in-game checks; synthetic and standalone checks are not exhaustive.
Automatic settings transfer requires a unique sibling .properties file with the historical seven-key core; ambiguous or incomplete configurations require manual selection.
GitHub update selection is covered by offline fixtures; the complete Mod Menu notification flow and settings screens require graphical client checks.
